assertion.statement: For an inflated normalized sign cocycle and a Dirichlet character with its local square boundaries, a continuous cochain eta in mu_(2m) satisfies eta^2=chi and delta(eta)=epsilon.
assertion.objects: A normalized sign cocycle epsilon inflated from Gal(L/Q), its chosen Dirichlet character chi of order m, and a finite scalar cochain eta.
assertion.hypotheses: L/Q is finite Galois and unramified outside the finite set T containing 2; the prescribed local order-two invariants determine chi.
assertion.quantifiers: For every element and pair of elements of G_Q; all finite places and the real place enter the class comparison.
assertion.parameter_range: No odd-order restriction on chi or the sign class; the same original L and T are retained.
assertion.uniformity: A single continuous cochain supplies the identity at every coefficient prime.
assertion.constants: eta takes values in mu_(2m), eta^2=chi, and delta(eta)=epsilon.
assertion.normalizations: Roots of unity are constant coefficient modules in the square sequence; eta is generally a cochain, not a character on G_Q.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The real invariant is forced by the global Brauer sequence. A nontrivial sign class is not discarded.
assertion.limit_order: Match local square boundaries, use global injectivity including infinity, then choose a finite continuous square-root cochain.

available_assertion.statement: A scalar degree-d nilsequence is uniformly approximable by a bounded linear combination of components of degree-d unit-vector nilcharacters. Nonzero degree-d bias is consequently witnessed by correlation with a degree-d nilcharacter.
available_assertion.objects: Scalar nilsequences, vector nilcharacters and their scalar components in the conventions of Section 6.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The degree-d nilsequence and bias hypotheses; the proof uses global ordinary vertical tests and the conjugation-stable point-separating algebra they generate.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Each fixed nilsequence and positive approximation tolerance; each biased sequence under the stated boundedness assumptions.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Fixed standard degree d; the current initial Section 7 use has d=s-1>0.
available_assertion.uniformity: The source gives a finite approximation for a fixed test; parameter-uniform finite witness lists are established in the local compact-net argument.
available_assertion.constants: Finite coefficient and geometry bounds must be retained when passing from approximation to positive component correlation.
available_assertion.normalizations: Correlation uses a selected scalar component of a globally unit vector; the vector is retained for subsequent symbol operations.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No claim that every weak object already satisfies the project strong convention; no prescribed-symbol selection is supplied.
available_assertion.limit_order: Construct ordinary approximants, take a finite net for the fixed bounded class, and only then choose a witness internally in the consuming proof.

assertion.statement: For genuine isogenies of abelian surfaces, degree is multiplicative and deg([n])=n^4 for nonzero integers n.
assertion.objects: Integral denominator-cleared isogenies [m]u and their compositions with multiplication maps on abelian surfaces.
assertion.hypotheses: Characteristic zero; m,n are positive integers for which the representatives are genuine isogenies.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such integral representative and positive m,n.
assertion.parameter_range: Genuine integral isogenies only; rational quasi-isogeny degree is subsequently defined and proved well-defined.
assertion.uniformity: The same degree law holds independently of coefficient prime and is unchanged by field conjugation.
assertion.constants: deg([n]([m]u))=n^4 deg([m]u).
assertion.normalizations: Degree is the rank of the finite locally free map; [-1] is a degree-one automorphism.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No degree assigned to [1/m] as an algebraic morphism; no rational discrepancy or finite cochain conclusion in this source input.
assertion.limit_order: Apply the integral theorem before dividing numerical degrees by m^4.

assertion.statement: Qualitative cofinite Frobenius equality extends to continuous conjugacy-invariant trace functions.
assertion.objects: Two continuous conjugacy-invariant trace functions on G_Q with values in one finite extension of Q_ell.
assertion.hypotheses: The functions agree on arithmetic Frobenius classes outside a finite set.
assertion.quantifiers: Every g in G_Q for each fixed pair of trace functions and each fixed coefficient prime ell.
assertion.parameter_range: The coefficient field carries its ell-adic topology; each density statement is for a finite quotient.
assertion.uniformity: No effective or simultaneous varying-field density bound is claimed.
assertion.constants: Only qualitative equality is concluded; no numerical Chebotarev constant is used.
assertion.normalizations: Conjugacy classes, continuous traces and the same arithmetic-Frobenius convention.
assertion.exceptional_cases: A finite comparison set may be omitted. Equality on a restricted subgroup alone would not suffice.
assertion.limit_order: Use finite-quotient Chebotarev to get dense conjugacy classes and then extend equality by continuity.

original_use.reason: Pass to each finite quotient for density and then use continuity in the fixed finite ell-adic coefficient extension. There is no effective bound or uniform varying-field assertion.

assertion.statement: The local boundary of the chosen finite character has exactly the prescribed order-two invariant.
assertion.objects: A finite character chi of G_Qp, the constant square sequence, and its boundary in Br(Q_p)[2].
assertion.hypotheses: Local reciprocity and the usual multiplicative decomposition of Q_p are used, rather than an arbitrary finite dyadic extension.
assertion.quantifiers: For every rational prime p and every continuous finite-order character chi.
assertion.parameter_range: Odd and dyadic p; no restriction on the finite order of chi.
assertion.uniformity: The criterion determines the order-two Brauer class for each p.
assertion.constants: The invariant is 0 if chi(-1)=1 and 1/2 if chi(-1)=-1.
assertion.normalizations: The roots-of-unity coefficients in the square sequence are constant; only mu_2 agrees with the natural coefficient module.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At p=2 use Q_2^*=2^Z times {1,-1} times (1+4Z_2); the full Brauer group is not a two-element group.
assertion.limit_order: Construct a character square root on each factor; its existence detects zero boundary, which determines Br(Q_p)[2].

original_use.reason: The local square-root criterion is chi(-1)=1 for Q_p, including p=2. Together with the two-element 2-torsion subgroup of the Brauer group this identifies the class, rather than only a necessary condition.

assertion.statement: The conditional scalar-commutant and semisimplicity calculation is valid over every finite coefficient extension.
assertion.objects: V_ell(A), the split quaternion action, and the original primitive matrix-unit factor r_ell.
assertion.hypotheses: L-prime is a number field defining all geometric endomorphisms, End^0(A_bar)=B, the normalized G_Q action commutes with B, and its G_L-prime restriction is actual Tate.

assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero coefficient fields; the non-CM full-End=B case.
assertion.uniformity: The geometric A and L-prime and the original factor remain fixed across coefficient primes.
assertion.constants: The rank-four commutant is M_2(E_lambda); the rank-two factor has commutant E_lambda.
assertion.normalizations: Use the original e_11. A change of matrix units is by an invertible quaternion element commuting with G_Q.
assertion.exceptional_cases: ell=2 is included. Merely knowing B is contained in the endomorphism algebra is insufficient.
assertion.limit_order: Apply Faltings, extend the finite linear commutant equations, preserve semisimplicity, and exclude nontrivial idempotents after every finite scalar extension.

original_use.reason: Faltings gives the commutant over the number field and semisimplicity. A finite linear system defining the commutant commutes with extension; separability in characteristic zero preserves semisimplicity. The primitive factor has scalar commutant, hence is absolutely irreducible. Its original G_Q action must commute with B.

assertion.statement: A nonconstant rational function on a nonempty rational affine open cannot take only integer values on its rational points.
assertion.objects: The composite of X1/X0 with the dominant rational parametrization of the actual quotient cubic.
assertion.hypotheses: The parametrization is dominant over Q; its domain meets the input chart in a nonempty open; X1/X0 is nonconstant.

assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.

assertion.normalizations: Shrink to a rational affine principal open avoiding the denominator. No density of rational points on the cubic itself is assumed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: Dominance preserves nonconstancy in function fields. Choose a real ball in the affine principal open. The numerator minus this constant times the denominator vanishes on a real open ball, hence identically, contradiction.
